task: 4.2 open-vocabulary perception (FastSAM-s segmentation + CLIP ViT-B/32 zero-shot labelling)
measurement_boundary: per-stage: request build + in-cluster round trip + server inference. Excludes Kafka. Same boundary as Task 4.1 so the numbers are comparable.
status: SPIKE -- hand-applied outside GitOps (Argo CD is not installed on this cluster). Not a supported deployment.

environment.serving_runtime: OpenVINO Model Server, image pinned by digest sha256:11d3acf...
environment.model_storage: pvc:// (one RWO PVC per model; cluster is EBS-only, no RWX)
environment.accelerator: none (CPU inference; this cluster has 0 GPU nodes)

models.fastsam: FastSAM-s OpenVINO IR FP32, in [1,3,640,640], out out_0 [1,37,8400] + input [1,32,160,160]
models.clip: CLIP ViT-B/32 OpenVINO IR FP32 via optimum-intel, dynamic batch

environment.decision_rule: argmax over 8 fixed prompts per segment; flag obstruction if any segment's argmax is an obstruction prompt

quality.score: 1/2 (50%) on the demo frames -- same score as YOLOv8 in Task 4.1, opposite failure mode

top_label: a wooden pallet blocking the aisle
results.note: Open vocabulary fixes the Task 4.1 false negative: 'pallet' is not a COCO-80 class, but CLIP names it correctly at 0.98.

top_label: a clear empty warehouse aisle floor
competing_label: a wooden pallet blocking the aisle
results.note: Decisive counterexample. Zero-shot CLIP has no 'none of these' option, so every segment is forced onto the nearest prompt. Background floor/rack segments get labelled as pallets at high confidence. This is a decision-rule defect, not evidence that open-vocabulary perception cannot work.

latency.verdict: FAIL, but by 2.1x rather than the 13-21x reported in Task 4.1
latency.headline: Fixing transport and HTTP client took the pipeline from 8282ms to 1062ms (7.8x) with no model change.

segment_count_sweep_total_ms.note: Even at 5 segments the floor is 639ms. Fixed costs dominate: FastSAM ~170ms, CLIP text tower re-encoded every call, and ~210ms of client-side preprocessing (letterbox, crop, resize, normalise) on a 2-CPU pod.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The Task 4.1 latency failure was attributed to YOLOv8. It was not a model property. Two client/transport defects accounted for ~92% of the wall clock, and they affect any model served this way.

defect_1_json_transport.description: KServe v2 JSON encodes 1.23M floats as decimal text.

defect_2_requests_library.description: Identical payload, same server. The `requests` library adds ~790ms of response-handling overhead on a 9.7MB response. urllib3 is what requests wraps.
defect_2_requests_library.effect: 5.9x faster by changing client library alone

server_side_truth.note: From OVMS's own Prometheus counters, diffed across a known request count. FastSAM inference is ~125ms on cluster CPU vs 62ms on an M3 Pro -- a 2x gap, entirely reasonable. The model was never the problem.

hypotheses_ruled_out: kube-proxy / Service indirection: identical timing via ClusterIP Service and pod IP directly (806.0ms vs 806.7ms unaccounted)
TCP slow-start / connection reuse: keep-alive Session made no difference (949.6ms vs 957.4ms)
predictor CPU starvation: raising the limit from 2 to 6 cores moved binary RTT only 1034.7ms -> 947.0ms
payload content: a zeros tensor timed the same as random data

serving_gotchas: OVMS returns any output you do NOT request as binary inline as JSON text in the response header. Requesting only out_0 produced a 17.86MB response and 1923ms, vs 9.71MB and 958ms when both outputs were requested binary. Request every output binary, then ignore what you don't need.

The FastSAM OpenVINO IR has unnamed output tensors locally (ov raises 'Attempt to get a name for a Tensor without names'), but OVMS assigns names on load. The mask-prototype output is confusingly named 'input'.

pvc:// storageUri with RWO storage deadlocks every rolling update: the new pod cannot attach the volume while the old pod holds it (Multi-Attach error). Needs RWX, an S3 backend, or a Recreate strategy.
CLIP ViT-B/32 IR is ~605MB; the 1Gi predictor memory limit used in Task 4.1 would OOM it.
known_gaps: Still only 2 demo frames. The agreed input set was >=10 images. An 80% accuracy gate cannot be meaningfully evaluated on 2 samples -- this applies to the Task 4.1 result equally.
The <500ms gate is specified end-to-end (camera->alert); this boundary excludes Kafka, so true E2E is higher.
Optimisations identified but NOT yet measured: precomputing CLIP text embeddings once (the text tower currently re-runs on every request), and reducing client-side preprocessing cost.
Cosmos Reason 2-8B baseline still not run.
Measured on CPU only; this cluster has 0 GPU nodes.
